data.gender_notes: Berengaria is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Basque mythology, Berengaria was a goddess of light, joy, and the bearer of good news. In Christian tradition, it may have derived from Latin berengarius, meaning 'bright, shining one'. The name Berengaria carries the meaning “Bearer of good news” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Berengaria usually hope their child will grow to embody bearer of good news and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Berengaria total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: ברנגאריה
in_hebrew.meaning: היא שומרת על החרב שלה להגן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ברנגאריה היא שם פרטי נשי שמקורו בשפה הגרמנית, והוא מורכב מהמילים 'ברן' שפירושו 'דוב' ו-'גאר' שפירושו 'חנית' או 'חרב'. השם ברנגאריה ניתן לאישה ששומרת על החרב שלה להגן, ויש לו קונוטציה של כוח, אומץ וגבורה. השם ברנגאריה מוזכר בתנ"ך ככינויה של אחת מנשותיו של המלך ריצ'רד הלב הארי, והוא נחשב לשם נוצרי מסורתי.

in_greek.name: Βερεγγαρία
in_greek.meaning: Αυτή που φυλάει το δόρυ της
in_greek.long_meaning: Βερεγγαρία είναι ένα γυναικείο όνομα που προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και αποτελείται από τις λέξεις 'bearn' που σημαίνει 'αρκούδα' και 'gari' που σημαίνει 'δόρυ' ή 'σπαθί'. Το όνομα Βερεγγαρία σημαίνει αυτή που φυλάει το δόρυ της, και έχει μια έννοια δύναμης, ανδρείας και ηρωισμού. Το όνομα Βερεγγαρία ήταν γνωστό στην αρχαία Εκκλησία και συνδέεται με την πριγκίπισσα Βερεγγαρία, κόρη του βασιλιά της Νεαπόλε.

in_latin.name: Berengaria
in_latin.long_meaning: Berengaria is a feminine given name derived from the Germanic languages, composed of 'bera' meaning 'bear' and 'gari' meaning 'spear' or 'pike'. The name Berengaria signifies she who protects her spear, conveying connotations of strength, bravery, and valor. Historically, Berengaria was used in the medieval period and was borne by several noblewomen, including the queen consort of King Richard I of England.

in_english.name: Berengaria
in_english.meaning: She who protects her spear with strength and courage
in_english.long_meaning: Berengaria is a Christian feminine given name originating from Germanic roots, specifically from 'bera' meaning 'bear' and 'gari' meaning 'spear'. The name signifies a strong and courageous woman who protects her faith and family. Historically, Berengaria was the name of a 12th-century queen consort of King Richard I of England, and it has been used in various Christian cultures. The name conveys a sense of bravery, loyalty, and devotion.

celebrity_usage: Berengaria of Navarre, daughter of Sancho VI of Navarre
data.cultural_impact: In Christian lore, Berengaria of Navarre is most commonly known for her role in the legend of the Holy Grail. As the bride of King Arthur, she was believed to have been taken to the sacred Grail by Joseph of Arimathea to be raised as a sacred virgin in Avalon. This association of Berengaria with the Grail lingers in literary and popular culture as a symbol of spiritual purity, sacrifice, and Loyalty within the knightly code.
data.spiritual_significance: The historical figure Berengaria of Navarre, like her Basque goddess namesake, carries a strong association with illumination and divine guidance. Additionally, her role in the Grail legends underscores her spiritual significance as an embodiment of unwavering devotion and faith. In Christian theology, she represents the redeeming power of the divine feminine. By embracing the light and wisdom that Berengaria symbolizes, we can illuminate our own spiritual paths and seek guidance from the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Berengaria, meaning "bringing light," symbolizes the inner illumination and guidance of the Holy Spirit in the journey of faith. This name invites us to let our light shine brightly, illuminating the world around us with love and compassion.
